parts.label: (a)(i)
parts.stem:
Chlorine dioxide undergoes the following reaction in aqueous solution.

$$2\text{ClO}_2 + 2\text{OH}^- \rightarrow \text{ClO}_2^- + \text{ClO}_3^- + \text{H}_2\text{O}$$

The initial rate of the reaction was measured at different initial concentrations of $\text{ClO}_2$ and $\text{OH}^-$. The table shows the results obtained.

| experiment | $[\text{ClO}_2]$ / $\text{mol dm}^{-3}$ | $[\text{OH}^-]$ / $\text{mol dm}^{-3}$ | initial rate / $\text{mol dm}^{-3}\text{s}^{-1}$ |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 1 | $1.25 \times 10^{-2}$ | $1.30 \times 10^{-3}$ | $2.33 \times 10^{-4}$ |
| 2 | $2.50 \times 10^{-2}$ | $1.30 \times 10^{-3}$ | $9.34 \times 10^{-4}$ |
| 3 | $2.50 \times 10^{-2}$ | $2.60 \times 10^{-3}$ | $1.87 \times 10^{-3}$ |
parts.text: Use the data in the table to determine the rate equation, showing the order with respect to each reactant. Show your reasoning.

parts.label: (a)(ii)
parts.text: Calculate the value of the rate constant, $k$, using the data from experiment 2. State its units.

parts.label: (c)(i)
parts.stem: Some reactions are catalysed by one of the products of the reaction. This is called autocatalysis. An example of autocatalysis is the reaction between acidified manganate(VII) ions, $\text{MnO}_4^-$, and ethanedioic acid, $(\text{CO}_2\text{H})_2$. $\text{Mn}^{2+}$ ions catalyse this reaction. The reaction is slow in the absence of a catalyst.
parts.text:
Balance the equation for this reaction.

$$\ldots\ldots\text{MnO}_4^- + \ldots\ldots\text{H}^+ + \ldots\ldots(\text{CO}_2\text{H})_2 \rightarrow \ldots\ldots\text{Mn}^{2+} + \ldots\ldots\text{CO}_2 + \ldots\ldots\text{H}_2\text{O}$$
